Credit Risk Credit risk is the risk that an issuer or other counterparty to an investment will not fulfill its obligations.
The University's investment policy mitigates credit risk by limiting investments to certificates of deposit issued by institutions insured by th e Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) and ensuring that the value of an investment in any single issuer does not exceed the FDIC insurance limit.
Concentration of Credit Risk Concentration of credit risk is the risk of loss attributed to the magnitude of the University’s investment in a single issuer.
The University's policy to limit this risk includes investing in multiple CDs across different federally insured depository institutions.

Interest Rate Risk Interest rate risk is the risk that changes in interest rates will adversely affect the fair value of an investment.
Since all CDs held by the University have maturities of less than one year, interest rate risk is minimized.

UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND (a Component Unit of the State of Rhode Island) Notes to the Financial Statements - Continued For the Year Ended June 30, 2025 (49) Benefit Provisions The level of benefits provided to participants is established by Chapter 36 -10 of the General Laws, which is subject to ame ndment by the General Assembly.
Member benefit provisions vary based on service credits accumulated at dates specified in various amendments to the General Laws outlining minimum retirement age, benefit accrual rates , and maximum benefit provisions.
In general, members accumulate service credits for each year of service subject to maximum benefit accruals of 80% or 75%.
For those hired after June 30, 2012, the benefit accrual rate is 1% per year with a maximum benefit accrual of 40%.
For members retiring on or after July 1, 2024, retiree benefit amounts are based on the average highest three consecutive years of compensation.
Members eligible to retire at September 30, 2009 may retire with 10 years of service at age 60 or after 28 years of service at any age.

The retirement eligibility age increases proportionately for other members reflecting years of service and other factors until it aligns with the Social Security Normal Retirement Age, which applies to any member with less than 5 years of service as of July 1, 2012.
Members are vested after 5 years of service.
The plan provides for survivor’s benefits for service-connected death and certain lump sum death benefits.
Joint and survivor benefit provision options are available to members.
Cost of living adjustments are provided to retirees based on statutory provisions (Section 36 -10-35 of the Rhode Island General Laws).
For members and/or beneficiaries of members who retired on or before June 30, 2012, cost of living adjustments are compu ted annually.
For members retiring on or after July 1, 2012, twenty-five percent (or 1/4th) of the cost-of-living adjustment is computed annually until the plan reaches a 75% funded status.
The full benefit adjustment is reinstated for all members upon the plan reaching the 75% funded status.
The plan also provides nonservice -connected disability benefits after five years of service, and service -connected disability benefits with no minimum service requirement.

Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: June 26, 2025 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of the Certain Documents Relative to the Development, Construction, and Financing of New University Housing Purpose of Submittal: To recommend the Board of Trustees Finance and Facilities Committee recommend approval to the Board of Trustees of the New University Housing (NUH) Project and authorize execution of documents for the development, construction, and financing of two new on- campus undergraduate student housing communities and one graduate student and family housing community at the University of Rhode Island.
Background: In late 2022, the University of Rhode Island engaged a planning team led by Scion Advisory Services, with architects from CannonDesign, to develop a Housing and Residential Life Housing Master Plan to transform URI housing.

This initiative align ed with URI’s strategic commitment to enhanc e the student experience by providing modern, affordable, and desirable living spaces.
The plan recommended that URI pursue a public-private-partnership (P3) to address immediate housing needs on the Kingston campus.
In May 2024, URI issued a public request for proposal for a development partner, and after a thorough vetting process, selected Gilbane Development Company (Gilbane) as its P3 partner.
In September 2024, the University entered into a Preliminary Development Agreement (PDA) with Gilbane.
In March 2025, the University approved the feasibility study conducted by Gilbane confirming that the project was feasible and would move forward.
Gilbane then selected, with URI’s concurrence, Provident to serve as the project 501(c)(3) partner.
PRG – RI Properties LLC, a single member limited liability company, was organized by Provident for the Project.
URI DevCo LLC, a single purpose subsidiary of Gilbane, was also organized for development of the Project.

In April 2025, URI DevCo, Provident, and Raymond James (underwriter) commenced the application process to issue debt through the Rhode Island Health and Education Building Corporation (RIHEBC).
The Project is summarized below.
Project Overview: Project Scope & Design: • Total Beds: 1,134 • Planned Housing Phases: o Occupancy in Fall 2027: 514 undergraduate beds o Occupancy in Fall 2028: 400 undergraduate beds o Occupancy in Fall 2028: 220 graduate beds

• Building Types: o Undergraduate Housing (Two Buildings): Apartment-style, single bedrooms in two- and four- bedroom units.
Modular construction. o Graduate Housing (Six Buildings + Community Center): Apartments with studio, one-bedroom, two-bedroom, and three-bedroom configurations.
Modular rebuild on existing foundations. o All buildings meet state code and URI design standards.
Financial Summary (rounded): • Total Project Cost: $231MM (as of June 2025). • URI Equity Contribution: The University may fund an equity contribution to the Project, the amount of which is currently subject to negotiation, and will be up to the amount authorized by the Board during executive session. • Rental Rates: Rental rates are within acceptable range to URI Housing and Residential Life, though may need to increase due to changes in market conditions. • Annual Rate Escalation: 3% • Expected Occupancy Rate: 95% • Debt Term: 40 years (all-in). • Debt Coverage Ratio: 1.2x or better (Senior Debt). • Residual Cash Flow to URI: $317MM over the term (NPV @ 5% = $63.7MM).

Document Approval Over the past several months, the University has negotiated and vetted several Project documents, three of which are being brought to the Board today for approval, and two of which are being shared for informational purposes.

These documents, listed below, are described in more detail in the enclosed Board of Trustees resolutions. • The Ground Lease between the University and the Provident , will extend for a term of up to 42 years and will contain provisions requiring the Project to be constructed in accordance with campus standards (for approval). • The Affiliation Agreement between the University and Provident , which outlines each entity’s obligations to the project (for approval). • The Interim Management Agreement between the University and URI DevCo LLC, which will allow the University to continue to manage the graduate student housing until the expected turnover date of May 2026, at which time it will be turned over to the Developer for demolition and re -construction (for approval). • The Turnkey Development Agreement between URI DevCo LLC and Provident, pursuant to which the Developer will implement the design, construction, and commissioning of the Project for a stipulated sum in accordance with plans approved by the University (for information). • The Project Management Agreement between Provident and Inwood Management, outlining operations and maintenance of the Student Housing Facilities (for information).

Next Steps Upon the Board’s approval of the Project and authorization to continue negotiating required documents, URI will finalize the negotiation and execute the relevant documents.
The Project is scheduled for financial close in September 2025, at which point the final Project budget will be determined.
We look forward to continued collaboration with Gilbane to ensure this critical project’s seamless and successful implementation.
